Record Class TrainingSettings

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.micronaut.runner.build.training.TrainingSettings
Record Components:
readinessPath - the path to GET until it answers 2xx, once the port accepts a connection; null when the accepted connection alone means ready
workloadPaths - the paths to GET in order, each of which must answer 2xx; when this and workloadCommand are both empty the driver sends one GET / and accepts any status below 500
workloadRepeat - how many times the whole list of workloadPaths is requested; at least 1
workloadCommand - a command and its arguments, run after the paths with "MICRONAUT_RUNNER_TRAINING_URL" set to the application's base URL; it must exit with status 0; empty for none
runToExit - whether the application ends by itself, as one that is not a server does; there is then no readiness check, no workload and no stop, and the application must exit with status 0 within readinessTimeout
stopPath - the path to POST to stop the application, where an orderly stop needs a request rather than a signal; null to destroy the process
jvmArgs - JVM arguments of the training launch, placed before the driver's own
environment - environment variables added to the training launch
portVariable - the environment variable that receives the free loopback port the application is to listen on
readinessTimeout - how long the application may take to become ready, or to exit with runToExit
workloadTimeout - how long the paths and the command may take together
stopTimeout - how long the application may take to exit once asked to, before it is killed
public record TrainingSettings(@Nullable String readinessPath, List<String> workloadPaths, int workloadRepeat, List<String> workloadCommand, boolean runToExit, @Nullable String stopPath, List<String> jvmArgs, Map<String,String> environment, String portVariable, Duration readinessTimeout, Duration workloadTimeout, Duration stopTimeout) extends Record
How a training run exercises the application: how the TrainingDriver knows it is ready, what it asks of it, and how it stops it.

A training run launches the application once, from the archive the build produced, to learn something from it: the classes it loads at startup, or a JDK cache. The settings describe the application, not the build tool, so both plugins map theirs onto this one record.

A path is the path of an HTTP request to the application on the loopback interface. It starts with / and may carry a query string.

Since:
1.0
